scope: finite exact microscopes for the first four F3 rows only
claim_boundary: These laws establish bounded interaction theorems and exact finite witnesses. They do not establish the G6 morphology-to-capability predictor, empirical universality, or monotone synergy.

rows.scope: finite cue-conditioned deterministic plan tree with no external memory
assumptions: the final correct branch is indexed by one of N equiprobable cue classes
the cue is unavailable after the initial observation
the agent has at most K persistent memory states
the planner can inspect at most D steps ahead while the obligation requires horizon H
success requires the exact cue-indexed terminal action
rows.theorem: Exact success is possible iff K >= N and D >= H. If K < N, at least two cue classes collapse by pigeonhole; if D < H, the terminal discriminator lies outside the declared planning reach. The two resources therefore form an AND threshold rather than substitutable scalar capacity.
rows.negative_twin: make the terminal action cue-independent; the memory threshold disappears while the planning-horizon requirement remains
rows.nearest_counterexample: allow an uncharged external cue store or reveal the cue again at the terminal node; K >= N is no longer necessary
rows.falsifier: an exact policy within this scope with K < N or D < H

rows.scope: finite obligation-preserving quotient of raw observations
assumptions: raw items X are partitioned by an abstraction q into C classes
all items in one class have identical future obligations
different required classes must remain distinguishable
rows.theorem: An obligation-preserving abstraction changes the exact retained-state requirement from the number of task-distinct raw items to the number C of quotient classes. A coarser quotient that merges obligation-distinct items is not a cheaper exact solution; it makes exact success impossible.
rows.negative_twin: assign a distinct obligation to every raw item; then C = |X| and abstraction yields no memory saving
rows.nearest_counterexample: if the quotient is chosen after seeing test labels, apparent compression can be leakage rather than an architecture-independent law
rows.falsifier: an exact no-external-memory realization needing fewer states than the task-distinct quotient index, or a proof-preserving quotient that merges two future-distinct obligations

rows.scope: repeated exact search on a fixed finite obligation family with a retained learned heuristic
assumptions: baseline verified search cost is B0 per query
heuristic-guided verified search cost is B1 per query
learning and retaining the heuristic costs L once
all costs share one frozen additive unit and B0 >= B1
the heuristic does not change correctness or verifier power
rows.theorem: Over r uses, retaining the learned heuristic is cheaper exactly when r(B0-B1) > L, ties when equal, and loses when smaller. Thus heuristic value is search burden removed, amortized against acquisition cost; with zero verified reduction it can never pay at positive L.
rows.negative_twin: set B1 = B0 while leaving L > 0; the heuristic strictly loses for every reuse count
rows.nearest_counterexample: if the heuristic changes error rate or verifier power, the one-coordinate cost comparison is incomplete and this theorem does not apply
rows.falsifier: a correctly metered instance satisfying the assumptions where the winner disagrees with the sign of r(B0-B1)-L

rows.scope: finite receiver decision with a compressed partner-type model and a finite message alphabet
assumptions: partner type is compressed into at most S social-model states
the received message alphabet has at most K symbols
the receiver gets no other side information
the correct action can depend on the ordered pair (partner type, message)
exact success requires preserving every obligation-distinct pair
rows.theorem: The receiver can condition on at most S*K social-state/message cells. If the task contains more than S*K obligation-distinct type-message pairs, exact success is impossible. The bound is tight when both encoders are injective on the required distinctions and the decoder maps each cell to its required action.
rows.strongest_parent: finite communication complexity plus sufficient social-state representation
rows.negative_twin: make the action independent of partner type; social-model cardinality drops out and only message distinctions matter
rows.nearest_counterexample: shared side information can refine receiver distinctions without consuming either declared S or K and therefore violates the scope
rows.falsifier: an exact receiver with more than S*K obligation-distinct cells under the stated information restriction
